title: One open/closed decomposition for arbitrary condensed coefficients
statement: For a scheme T with noetherian underlying space, a commutative condensed ring Λ, and a constructible module M over the induced pro-etale coefficient ring, either M[0] is a condensed locally closed piece, or there is a nonsurjective closed immersion i:Z→T with exact closed pushforward, a constructible module MZ on Z, and a distinguished triangle A→M[0]→D(i_*)(MZ[0])→A[1], where A is a condensed locally closed piece. A piece is closed pushforward of quasi-compact open extension by zero of a locally finitely presented module, up to isomorphism.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and finite-stratum induction in the proof of Lemma 6.8.12

proof.text: Apply generic local finite presentation. If M is already locally finitely presented, identity open and closed immersions exhibit M[0] as a piece. Otherwise choose its nonempty locally finitely presented open U. The closed subscheme defined by the vanishing ideal of U complement gives a nonsurjective closed immersion i:Z→T.

Constructible pullback gives constructible MZ=i* M. Open/closed recollement supplies exact closed pushforward i_* and its bounded-below triangle. Map it to the ordinary derived category and use exact-functor single comparisons to identify its first object with j!j* M[0], its middle object with M[0], and its last with D(i*)(MZ[0]). Transport the triangle across these isomorphisms. Identity closed immersion exhibits the first object as a piece. The profinite-point identity comparisons identify identity closed pushforward and identity open restriction with the identity functor.
